## Overview

Separate physical PCP topology from layer backend requirements and per-forward attention layout in Model Runner V2. Replicated DFlash/DSpark drafts retain valid PCP/DCP topology instead of rewriting PCP size to one.

**Draft: constructor, metadata and distributed component checks pass; successful end-to-end generation and model evaluation remain pending.**

## Claims

- Preserve physical world size and DCP KV ownership when constructing replicated drafts. TP1/PCP4/DCP4 previously becomes TP1/PCP1/DCP4 and fails configuration validation.
- Carry an explicit PCP attention context through normal and capture/profile batches, so cache gathering follows the current forward layout instead of tensor-length heuristics.
- Separate repeated PCP query heads from distinct TP head shards in MLA/DCP metadata and workspace sizing.

## Validation

Base: `5689c2790c911a55c75825aac5166305df0b591d`; head: `81508ac804`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing PCP manager and non-causal MLA suites on H20 | 111 passed, 14 warnings |
| Real DSpark constructor, TP1/PCP4/DCP4 | Base fails divisibility validation; branch passes |
| Three capture-layout regression cases | Fail on base, pass on branch |
| Two-H20 NCCL probes | Three local/partitioned transitions, empty-owner gather and mixed cache mapping pass on both ranks |
| Two-H20 replicated PCP2/DCP2 combine | Weighted output and empty/NaN shard checks pass |
| Static checks | Ruff check/format passes on 47 Python files; native manual hooks pass except Linux-shell hooks unavailable on this Windows host (see limitations) |
| Layer PCP backend requirement | 1 passed; restoring the upstream selector makes the new test fail |
| V4.1 compressor metadata, PCP and cache synchronization | 21 passed on H20, including PCP2/PCP4 and auxiliary-stream graph cases |
| Dummy LLM, PCP2/DCP2/DSpark | Passes the former config failure, then fails backend selection on H20 |
| Model accuracy, acceptance, graph replay and performance | Not validated |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py -q --disable-warnings
pre-commit run --from-ref 5689c2790c911a55c75825aac5166305df0b591d \
  --to-ref 81508ac804 --hook-stage manual
```

Current layer validation ran on two idle H20 GPUs using a source overlay over image `sha256:f0fc75212b96dbfe01fa2ede5ab4cfbf140cf4270778b569b2d5ef238eb98c9a`. The broader compressor suite reaches NVFP4 kernels unsupported on H20 (`cvt .e2m1x2` on `sm_90a`). Full manual checks are limited by unavailable Linux shell/WSL; actionlint environment installation also stalled, with no workflow files changed. These are not claimed as passing.

The distributed probes and cropped dummy-model configurations were local experiment artifacts, not new CI model tests. The affected test coverage is wired into Buildkite.

The dummy model used a cropped GLM target and native K3 MLA DSpark draft, dummy weights, TP1/PCP2/DCP2, `ag_rs`, block size 64 and eager execution. The selector reaches `use_pcp=False, use_dcp=True, use_non_causal=True`: Triton MLA rejects non-causal MLA with DCP and FlashInfer MLA rejects H20's compute capability. A separate PCP2/DCP1 attempt fails at the precompiled `concat_and_cache_mla` ABI (six arguments available versus seven required); the isolated baseline reproduces that ABI failure. These attempts do not establish model correctness.

## Details

`prefill_context_parallel_size` continues to describe process topology. Each attention layer declares its backend PCP requirement through `use_pcp`; replicated draft layers request a local-input backend. Physical communication and DCP head ownership retain the original topology. Per-forward `PCPAttentionContext` travels through `InputBatch` and common attention metadata. MLA, indexer and V4.1 compressor/cache metadata consume the current forward layout, including padded/empty owners.

This spans shared configuration, MLA/indexer metadata and model capability checks. The rendered context-parallel deployment documentation describes the distinction. Partitioned K3 target support is still gated; allowing a replicated K3 draft does not establish PCP support for the K3 target.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-11-04 searched open PCP, DSpark and PCP-topology PRs. No matching topology/execution separation was found. Related #61994 (merged) synchronizes replicated DSpark proposals; #54036 optimizes draft context-KV precompute; #64261 enables a non-causal Triton MLA DCP backend on gfx942. Those address different layers of the problem.

Before readiness: successful generation on a commit-aligned compatible runtime; graph replay and nonzero draft acceptance; token/logit consistency and model evaluation; performance and other-platform qualification; human line-by-line review and confirmation of validation. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing and this description.

+### Topology and attention execution layout
+
+`ParallelConfig.prefill_context_parallel_size` describes the physical PCP group.
+It participates in world-size and DCP topology validation even when a draft
+model repeats its queries on every PCP rank. Attention layers declare whether
+their backend needs to support PCP-partitioned inputs through the layer's
+`use_pcp` constructor argument. Replicated draft layers select a rank-local
+backend with `use_pcp=False`, while retaining the physical PCP and DCP groups.
+This argument constrains backend selection; metadata describes each forward's
+actual input layout.
+
+Each partitioned forward carries `CommonAttentionMetadata.pcp_context`, including
+capture and profiling forwards. Builders propagate this into backend metadata,
+and cache writers use it to decide whether to gather partitioned KV rows.
+A missing context means rank-local input, including a replicated draft forward.
+Tensor lengths validate a declared layout; they do not choose the layout.
+
+DCP KV ownership and query-head communication remain tied to physical topology.
+For PCP greater than one, DCP equal to PCP repeats the same TP heads; DCP equal
+to TP times PCP combines distinct TP head shards. Backend schedules and workspace
+sizes count distinct heads, not duplicated PCP copies. Replicated attention does
+not imply replicated KV when DCP is enabled.
+
+For example, a target with TP=1, PCP=4 and DCP=4 retains that topology in its MLA
+draft configuration while the draft executes locally on each rank. This removes
+the invalid intermediate TP=1, PCP=1, DCP=4 configuration. Model and backend
+capability restrictions still apply: the K3 target does not support partitioned
+PCP, and non-causal multi-token MLA with DCP requires a backend explicitly
+supporting that combination. This separation alone does not enable new kernels.
+
 ## Decode Context Parallel
 
 Due to the auto-regressive nature of decoding, every decoding step needs to compute a small amount of query tokens w.r.t. a large number of key/value tokens stored in the paged KV cache. The core of decode context parallel is how to shard the KV cache across GPUs.
